ca_central_wall.blurb: Central Wall is one of the walls of the Main Formation at Lover's Leap, the big cliff near Strawberry, west of South Lake Tahoe. It sits between the East Wall and the Main Wall. All ten routes here are trad, and most are long multi-pitch lines of three to five pitches. Grades start at 5.7, with a couple of 5.8s, then a solid group at 5.10 and a harder cluster at 5.11, so it suits parties who are comfortable on sustained leads. The cliff as a whole stands up to 600 feet tall. Bring a full trad rack and plan for a long day on the wall.

ca_castle_grey_skull.blurb: Castle Grey Skull is a small crag on the south side of Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains, at roughly 7,500 feet, off a Forest Service spur road that leaves Mill Creek Road. The walk from the end of the road is brief, about five to ten minutes. The crag holds ten routes of short pitches, with the bulk in the 5.10 range, a pair of 5.11s, and a few easier lines between 5.6 and 5.9. Every route can be top-roped by scrambling up a gully on the east side. Bring your own protection and slings to build longer anchors.

ca_caveman_boulder.blurb: Caveman Boulder is a large boulder in the HVCG West sector of the Hidden Valley Campground bouldering circuit in Joshua Tree National Park. It is known for a cave with a roof, and its headline problem starts on the right side of the cave and traverses left under the roof. Ten problems cover a wide spread: six are easy to moderate, between VB and V3, followed by a few hard lines around V6 and V7 and a single V10 at the top end. It works for a mixed group, with warm-up problems beside serious projects. Bring pads.

ca_broken_boulder_the.blurb: The Broken Boulder is a small bouldering spot in the AFPA Rock area of Joshua Tree National Park's Quail Springs section, directly across the road from the Trashcan Rock picnic area. Its ten problems are gentle overall: a handful at VB to V0, four at V1, then a couple of V4s and one V5. Faces include blunt aretes and slopers, with at least some landings flat. Boulders run roughly fifteen to twenty feet tall, so bring pads and a spotter. A good stop for people newer to bouldering or anyone looking for easy volume next to the road.

ca_2nd_tier.blurb: 2nd Tier is an east-facing wall in the Tiers section of Cloudburst Canyon, part of Woodfords Canyon off Highway 88 near Carson Pass. It holds ten gear-protected routes, nearly all of them moderate: one 5.8, four 5.9s and four 5.10s, plus a single 5.12. The canyon has a creek that flows year-round and offers shade, and the walk from the dirt parking area takes around ten to fifteen minutes. The moderate grades and single-pitch lines make it a reasonable choice for climbers building trad skills, though a few lines are spicier than their number suggests.

ca_bear_island.blurb: Bear Island is a small rock in the North Wonderland Approach part of Joshua Tree National Park, a short distance northwest of the Boy Scout trail. From the trailhead lot it is a flat walk of roughly fifteen to twenty minutes. Ten routes are here: eight trad, one sport and one top-rope. Most lines are easy, from 5.3 to 5.9, with a single 5.12 sport route as the outlier, and the rock top-ropes readily. Climbers describe it as secluded and quiet, and it sits in the sun for much of the day, making it a good pick for beginners and anyone avoiding crowds.
